mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi engine typically costs £1,800-£3,500 supply-only, depending on power output and supplier. DW10FC 150hp units start around £1,800, while 177hp units range £2,000-£3,500. Used engines start from £1,200. Supply & fit adds £500-£900 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £6,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) engine problems are AdBlue injector crystallisation triggering countdowns (€1,200-€1,400 repair cost), high-pressure fuel pump leaks causing low rail pressure and no-start, DPF blockage from short-journey driving (£1,200+ DPF replacement), and injector coding and contribution faults (P0266/P0269). The DW10FC is generally a robust engine capable of exceeding 300,000 km, but its Euro 6 emissions systems require careful maintenance.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound. A rebuilt unit costs £1,800-£3,500 versus £4,000-£12,000 for a comparable used 308. With dealer replacement potentially exceeding £6,500, specialist rebuilt units offer significant savings. The 2.0 BlueHDi's strong torque and towing capability make it a desirable engine - replacement often makes sense for well-maintained GT and GT Line examples. The DW10FC block is robust and can exceed 300,000 km, making it a worthwhile investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) engine typically reaches 150,000-200,000 miles (300,000 km+). Regular oil changes with 5W-30 PSA B71 2312 specification, DPF-friendly driving (regular motorway runs) and AdBlue system maintenance are essential for longevity. The timing belt requires replacement at 180,000 km or 10 years. The DW10FC block is robust and well-engineered, but its emissions systems demand vigilance.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi and 2.0 HDi engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) is a Euro 6 diesel introduced in 2014, featuring AdBlue (SCR) for lower NOx emissions. The older 2.0 HDi (DW10BTED4/RHR) is a Euro 5 diesel from 2007-2013 without AdBlue. Both use the same 2.0L (1,997cc) DW10 architecture, but the BlueHDi has more complex emissions hardware and is generally more fuel-efficient. The BlueHDi is also more sensitive to short-journey driving patterns due to its DPF and AdBlue systems.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi engine code is DW10FC (AHW / EHZ). It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. The 150hp variant uses code AHW and the 177hp variant uses EHZ. historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) is the performance diesel engine for the second-generation (Phase 2, 2013-2021) 308, delivering strong torque, excellent motorway cruising and impressive towing capability. Part of Stellantis's DW10 engine family, the 2.0 BlueHDi produces 150hp or 177hp and offers the best balance of power and economy for GT, GT Line and high-spec trims. Available from 2014 to 2021, it powers Allure, GT Line and GT variants - but its complex AdBlue system, DPF maintenance requirements and injector vulnerabilities have made it a source of replacement enquiries for high-mileage examples.

milestones.description: **2014** - Second-generation 308 launched with DW10FC (AHW) 2.0 BlueHDi 150hp and 177hp
**2015** - Minor ECU refinements to improve DPF regeneration and cold-start behaviour
**2016** - DW10FC continues as the performance diesel option for GT and GT Line trims
**2017** - AdBlue system updates introduced to address crystallisation issues; Peugeot recall (code HUH) for AdBlue tank breather valve
**2019** - WLTP testing leads to ECU calibration updates across all DW10FC variants
**2021** - Phase 2 production ends; 2.0 BlueHDi discontinued in favour of 1.5 BlueHDi and PHEV powertrains

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every DW10FC engine fitted to the Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) is a robust, high-torque diesel - but its complex emissions hardware and high-mileage wear patterns create distinct failure points. AdBlue injector crystallisation, high-pressure fuel pump leaks, DPF blockage and injector coding failures are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. The DW10 family is generally considered a robust engine block, capable of exceeding 300,000 km, but its Euro 6 emissions systems demand careful maintenance. Every rebuilt Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: AdBlue Injector Failure - Why Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi Engines Trigger Countdowns and White Steam
problems.rootCause: Crystallised urea deposits clog the AdBlue injector nozzle, triggering fault codes and eventually a countdown to engine immobilisation. The AdBlue system is sensitive to temperature variations - crystallisation is more common in cold conditions and on vehicles used for short journeys. The AdBlue tank breather valve can also become blocked, causing the tank to deform under vacuum (recall HUH). Crystallised AdBlue can also contaminate the DPF, as regens do not burn off urea crystals effectively. Fault code P20E8 (low AdBlue system pressure) is a common indicator.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injector, ultrasonic clean, system reset, test drive
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before countdown reaches zero; some owners report DIY cleaning success

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply and fit new AdBlue injector, recalibrate system
repairOptions.longevity: Restores function; may need tank flush if contamination severe; AdBlue injector replacement can cost €1,200-€1,400

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new emissions hardware, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if injector failure led to NOx damage or engine derate

problems.recommendation: Address AdBlue warnings immediately - a £120-£300 specialist clean can prevent a £700+ injector replacement. If the countdown has started, act fast to avoid immobilisation. Replacement engines are only needed if the fault caused secondary damage. The 2.0 BlueHDi's AdBlue system is sensitive to short-journey driving - regular longer runs help prevent crystallisation.

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - Why Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi Engines Lose Pressure and Fail to Start
problems.rootCause: The HPFP can develop leaks at the leak-off return port, allowing air to enter the fuel system. This prevents the pump from building the required rail pressure (350-370 bar requested, but only 10-120 bar achieved), causing the engine to fire briefly and die. Air ingress can be heard as a hissing noise from the leak-off return port. Injector coding can also fail if the ECU detects low rail pressure or air in the system.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace high-pressure fuel pump, leak-off pipe, fuel filter, system bleed and prime
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before injectors are damaged; requires correct coding of new injectors

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new HPFP, injectors and fuel system, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if HPFP failure has caused injector or rail damage

problems.recommendation: HPFP failure on the Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi is often caused by air ingress through the leak-off return port. If you hear a hissing noise from the HPFP area or the engine struggles to start, have the fuel system inspected immediately. Replacing the HPFP and leak-off pipe early can prevent injector damage. If metallic debris has contaminated the fuel system, a full rebuilt engine is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DW10FC Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi engine prices

problems.h4: DPF Blockage - Why Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi Engines Trigger Anti-Pollution Faults
problems.rootCause: Short-journey driving prevents the DPF from reaching regeneration temperature, causing soot buildup that blocks exhaust flow and triggers anti-pollution warnings. The 2.0 BlueHDi's DPF is sensitive to urban driving patterns, and regeneration requires sustained motorway speeds to complete effectively. AdBlue crystallisation can also contaminate the DPF, as regens do not burn off urea crystals effectively. Oil dilution can occur during multiple regen attempts. DPF replacement at a dealer can cost £1,200+.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic reset, extended high-speed drive or forced regen cycle
repairOptions.longevity: Works if blockage is early-stage and sensors are functional

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove DPF for off-car cleaning or supply fitted replacement unit
repairOptions.longevity: Restores function if substrate isn't melted or cracked; DPF replacement at dealer can cost £1,200+

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new DPF and EGR components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Needed if blockage caused turbo or piston damage

problems.recommendation: For a Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi used mainly for short trips, invest in regular motorway runs to allow DPF regeneration. The 2.0 BlueHDi's DPF is larger and more robust than the 1.6L unit, but still requires attention. If the anti-pollution warning appears, address it promptly. A rebuilt engine is only necessary if the DPF has caused turbo or internal damage - the DW10FC block is generally robust and can be saved if caught early. Check for AdBlue crystallisation as a potential cause of DPF contamination.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DW10FC Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi engine prices

problems.h4: Injector Coding & Contribution Faults - Why Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi Engines Run Rough
problems.rootCause: Injector seals degrade over time, allowing combustion gases to leak and carbonise around the injector seat. Fault codes P0266 and P0269 (cylinder contribution) are common indicators. Injector coding can fail if the ECU detects low rail pressure or air in the system. The 2.0 BlueHDi's injectors require precise coding using Bosch-certified diagnostic equipment.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removal of faulty injectors, replacement with new or reconditioned units, ECU coding
repairOptions.longevity: Effective; prevents further oil dilution and rough running

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new injectors and seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if injector failure has caused cylinder head damage

problems.recommendation: Injector coding and contribution faults on the Peugeot 308 2.0 BlueHDi should be addressed promptly. If you notice rough idle, clattering noises or loss of power, have the injector coding checked. A specialist can replace faulty injectors and code them to the ECU. If cylinder head damage is confirmed from gas leakage, a rebuilt engine may be more cost-effective. The DW10FC's injectors are high-precision components - always use Bosch-certified equipment for coding.
